comparison: Both evaluate LC responses to auditory stimuli (C31-C34). OpenEval finds the fiber photometry data convincing with appropriate statistical support. Peer reviewers praised this work as 'convincing' and offering 'unprecedented account' of neural signals to different tone intensities. Strong agreement on support for these claims.

Both address LC responses to aversive stimuli (C35-C37). OpenEval finds strong statistical evidence for intensity-dependent responses. Peer reviewers praised the examination of different shock intensities as part of the 'unprecedented account.' Both evaluations support these claims.

Both evaluate synthesis claims about intensity-dependent LC responses (C38-C39). OpenEval notes appropriate caveats about separating salience from valence. Peer reviewers found the overall neural profiling 'convincing' without raising concerns about this interpretation. Agreement on support.

Both address habituation findings (C41-C44). OpenEval notes clear statistical support for tone onset habituation with appropriate reporting of non-significant tone termination effect. Peer reviewers specifically praised the examination of repeated tone presentation (habituation) as 'unprecedented.' Strong agreement.

Both evaluate associative learning and extinction effects (C46-C53). OpenEval finds strong statistical support with appropriate interaction analysis. Peer reviewers praised the conditioning examination as offering 'unprecedented account' with no concerns raised. Complete agreement on support.

Both address LC activity during trace fear conditioning (C55-C58). OpenEval notes strong statistical support with appropriate handling of marginal tone termination result. Peer reviewers found data 'convincing' in documenting LC responses to cue onset, offset, and shock. Agreement on support.

Both evaluate LC-HPC projection activity (C59-C61). OpenEval highlights strong evidence from larger sample size and statistical confirmation at all time points. Peer reviewers noted the timing of LC activity is well-supported without raising concerns. Agreement on support.

Perfect claim overlap (C63-C67) on optogenetic memory enhancement. OpenEval finds appropriate controls and strong statistical support. Peer reviewers specifically highlighted 'Excellent use of data acquired with fiber photometry in the optogenetic interrogation study.' Complete agreement on strong support.

Both address co-release of neurotransmitters (C70-C74). OpenEval notes strong statistical support with appropriate caveats about indirect DA release. Peer reviewers praised the use of pharmacology to disentangle dopamine and norepinephrine as 'excellent.' Agreement on support despite OpenEval noting some uncertainty about mechanisms.

Perfect claim overlap (C75-C81) on norepinephrine pharmacology. OpenEval finds converging negative results across multiple approaches, noting consistency but some surprise given other literature. Peer reviewers praised the pharmacology as 'excellent' and accepted that norepinephrine is not critical. Agreement on support.

Both evaluate dopamine necessity findings (C83-C87). OpenEval finds strong convergent evidence from systemic and site-specific pharmacology. Peer reviewers stated pharmacology 'revealed that dopamine and not norepinephrine are critical' and found data 'convincing.' Strong agreement.

Both address encoding vs. consolidation distinction (C89-C91). OpenEval notes good evidence but suggests additional time points would strengthen conclusion. Peer reviewers accepted the encoding-specific role without questioning the temporal distinction. Agreement on support with OpenEval slightly more cautious.

Both evaluate hippocampal DA release mirroring LC activity (C92-C94). OpenEval finds strong statistical support with good sample size. Peer reviewers noted the timing of hippocampal dopamine release is 'convincing' and well-supported. Agreement on support.

Both address DA release timing during learning (C95-C96). OpenEval finds strong statistical support at all time points. Peer reviewers found the timing data 'convincing' without concerns. Agreement on support.

Both evaluate prediction error analysis (C97-C100). OpenEval notes the pattern is inconsistent with classical prediction error signaling and suggests more trials needed. Peer reviewers praised the 'deconstruction of the elements of conditioning' without raising concerns about interpretation. Peer reviewers more supportive than OpenEval.

Both address signaled vs. unsignaled shock experiment (C101-C102). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to very small sample size (n=5) and low statistical power. Peer reviewers accepted findings without raising power concerns. Disagreement: OpenEval uncertain, peer reviewers supportive.

Both evaluate interpretation of LC-driven DA release (C74). OpenEval finds interpretation reasonable with appropriate caveats about alternative mechanisms. Peer reviewers found the dopaminergic input conclusion 'convincing' without concerns about indirect mechanisms. Agreement on support.
OpenEval evaluates basic methodology (C30) showing GCaMP6s expression confirmation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this methodological claim.
OpenEval evaluates literature context and rationale claims (C1-C29). These background claims establish knowledge gaps. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation of these contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluates contextualization claims (C45, C54) that relate findings to prior work. Peer R2 includes C45 and C54 in broader evaluation of habituation/conditioning findings, finding them part of 'unprecedented account.' Agreement on support.

OpenEval evaluates inference about LC-HPC importance (C62) as reasonable but correlational until causal evidence provided. Peer R3 includes C62 in evaluation supporting that LC input is 'key instigator' of conditioning. Agreement on support with OpenEval more cautious about causal language.

OpenEval evaluates discussion section claims (C68-C129) as appropriately interpreting findings in light of prior work with accurate citations. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation of these discussion interpretations.

OpenEval rates mechanistic speculation claims (C109-C135) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are plausible hypotheses appropriately qualified but lacking direct experimental support. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these speculative claims.
OpenEval evaluates discussion summary claims (C110-C124) as well-supported synthesis of experimental findings. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation of these summary claims.
